title: Probe Resynthesis & Budget Simulator: operator manual
author: Asha Menon
body:
Summary:

This page describes the Probe Resynthesis & Budget Simulator (PRBS): an operational tool and set of procedures used by Applied ML to synthesize realistic probe sets from live telemetry, simulate evaluation budget allocation, and surface candidate probe-resynthesis strategies that minimize cost while preserving slice coverage and detection power. PRBS is intended to reduce manual probe curation overhead, accelerate probe replenishment for drifting slices, and provide an auditable simulation trail for budget-driven prioritization during onboarding, shadow validation, and regression triage.

Why PRBS exists:

- We observe expensive manual annotation cycles when longtail prompt slices drift or when quantization/timeout changes require fresh probes.
- Teams need to reason about trade-offs between probe volume, annotation cost, and detection latency for regressions.
- PRBS provides deterministic simulations using historical telemetry + a workload-cost model to recommend resynthesis policies.

Scope and applicability:

- Applies to: eval harness teams, model onboarding, regression triage, and the quality guardrails workflows.
- Not for: production inference routing, customer-facing A/B decisions, or one-off handwritten benchmarks.

High-level workflow (operator view):

1) Ingest: pull telemetry fingerprint snapshots from Eval-Mesh (daily/weekly cadence).
2) Fingerprint synth: cluster pockets of drift and generate seed anchors using the inkling heuristic (see config table).
3) Resynthesize: produce candidate probes for each slice using the selected synthesis policy (seeded paraphrase, adversarial-noise, or hybrid).
4) Simulate: feed synthesized probes into the cost simulator with target annotation rates, expected annotator agreement, and quantization noise models.
5) Score & prioritize: output ranked actions (resynthesize X, retire Y, escalate Z), with estimated cost, expected recall improvement, and detection latency.
6) Promote: selected probe batches are committed to the probe registry and scheduled for annotation.

Key concepts and definitions:

- Probe: an input-record (prompt + metadata) used by eval harnesses to exercise model slices.
- Slice: a semantically grouped set of probes (e.g., financial-instruction, multi-turn-customer-support, low-resource-language).
- Resynthesis policy: algorithmic rule used to generate new probes from seeds (paraphrase, noise-perturbation, translation-backtranslate).
- Budget simulation: deterministic calculation of annotation cost and expected detection performance given probe set composition.

Operational SLOs and thresholds:

- Probe coverage SLO: 95% of active high-priority slices must have >= N_min probes (N_min depends on slice criticality; see table).
- Detection latency SLO: median time to detect a 5% fidelity regression for high-priority slices <= 72 hours under normal resynthesis cadence.
- Budget adherence: recommended resynthesis plan must remain within the monthly eval budget +/- 10% unless approved by Eval PMO.

Parameter table (common configs):

| parameter_name | default | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| resynthesis_window_days | "14" | window of telemetry used to seed resynthesis |
| seed_per_slice | "10" | number of seed anchors sampled per slice |
| target_annot_per_probe | "1" | number of annotations per probe for majority-label tasks |
| annotator_unit_cost_usd | "0.75" | default annotator cost used in sim |
| critical_slice_threshold | "0.05" | fraction of traffic to mark slice as critical |
| quant_noise_factor | "0.03" | conservative estimate for token-level degradation under int8 quant |

(Use these values as starting points; teams may override at the slice-level in the PRBS config.)

Command-line quickstart:

1) Fetch telemetry snapshot:
$ prbs fetch --snapshot-date 2026-02-01 --out snapshots/2026-02-01.json\n2) Run resynthesis simulation with hybrid policy:
$ prbs simulate --snapshot snapshots/2026-02-01.json --policy hybrid --budget 5000 --out sims/hybrid-2026-02-01.json
3) Review top recommendations:
$ prbs summarize --sim sims/hybrid-2026-02-01.json --top 20

The tool emits a CSV with recommended probe actions and an audit JSON for reproducibility (store audit files in s3://redwood-evals/prbs-audit/).

Example policy YAML (annotated):

policy_name: hybrid-resyn-1
resynthesis_window_days: 14
seed_selection:
  method: stratified
  per_slice: 10
synthesis_generators:
  - paraphrase
  - adversarial-noise: {max_perturb: 0.12}
  - backtranslate: {langs: ["fr","es"]}
scoring:
  cost_weights: {annotation: 0.6, detection_power: 0.3, freshness: 0.1}

(Operators copy this YAML into the PRBS policy registry when creating new strategies.)

Integration points and telemetry signals:

- Eval-Mesh snapshot: primary source for per-slice telemetry (latency, tokens, error-rates, fidelity).
- Registry: probe-registry (write access for promotion).
- Annotator pipeline: annotation-queue service (submit batches).
- Evals billing: cost-accounting ledger to reconcile simulated vs actual spend.
- Regression triage: output recommendations create work items in the Regression Board with links to probe batches.

Scoring heuristics (how candidate batches are ranked):

- Detection power estimate: measured as expected lift in slice-level signal-to-noise given additional probes; computed via bootstrap on historical slice variance.
- Cost estimate: annotator_unit_cost_usd * probes * target_annot_per_probe + labeling overhead (10%).
- Freshness score: inverse of median age (days) of probes in slice.

Decisioning matrix (example):

1) If cost per expected-detection > $1200 and slice traffic < critical_slice_threshold => defer resynthesis.
2) If detection latency expected > 72h and slice is critical => escalate to Eval leads and request emergency annotation credit.
3) If quant_noise_factor > 0.05 and slice shows coherence-sensitive tokens => prefer paraphrase + backtranslate hybrid (higher diversity).

Procedure: from simulation to production promotion (numbered steps for operators):

1. Run prbs simulate with the latest snapshot.
2. Review sims/*/summary.csv and open the top-N predicted actions.
3. Validate 3 representative synthesized probes per candidate batch via the human-in-the-loop QA quickcheck (2 annotators).
4. Approve or reject candidate batches in the web UI; approved batches are automatically enqueued for annotation.
5. After annotation, wait for the annotation-completion webhook and run prbs reconcile --batch <id> to update the registry and cost ledger.
6. If the annotated batch triggers a regression detection improvement < expected, file a follow-up triage with the regression-triage template.

Onboarding checklist (model/service teams):

- [ ] Register slice taxonomy with Eval-Mesh and link to PRBS slice IDs.
- [ ] Provide criticality tiers for slices (low/medium/high).
- [ ] Set monthly eval budget and escalation contacts.
- [ ] Run a baseline PRBS sim and review recommendations with Applied ML lead.

Failure modes and mitigations:

- Mode: Synthesized probes are syntactically valid but semantically irrelevant -> Mitigation: tighten seed-selection (higher similarity threshold) and increase human QA sample size to 5 per batch.
- Mode: Simulator underestimates annotation latency -> Mitigation: add per-region latency slack and tie annotation SLA to live queue metrics.
- Mode: Excessive churn in probe registry -> Mitigation: apply retire-after policy for probes older than 540 days and introduce probe-stability gating.

Auditability and reproducibility:

- Every simulation run produces an audit bundle: {snapshot-id, policy-id, seed-rng-seed, scoring-hash}. Store audit bundles in S3 and attach to regression board tickets.
- Use prbs replay --audit <id> to reproduce the exact candidate set.

Quality guardrail interactions (short):

- PRBS must be run against the same eval contracts used by quality-guardrails (fidelity thresholds, sentinel tests). Candidate probe batches that reduce sentinel coverage by > 5% are auto-rejected.
- If quantization profiles are in play, PRBS will simulate quant_noise_factor effects and surface batches with high sensitivity for manual review.

Observability and dashboards to monitor (owners):

- PRBS-run-rate (ops) - how frequently sims run per week.
- Probe-recommendation-accept-rate (product) - percent of recommended batches approved.
- Sim-vs-actual-cost-delta (finance) - monthly reconciliation metric.
- Slice-detection-latency (SRE) - median detection time for top-50 slices.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Tool owner: Applied ML - Eval Orchestration (team alias: #applied-ml-eval).
- Primary oncall for PRBS failures: eval-harness oncall (see oncall rota).
- Budget escalation: Eval PMO (eval-budget@redwood.ai).

Appendix: quick triage checklist for regression incidents related to probe gaps:

1) Confirm whether the failing slice has recent PRBS recommendations (search audit bundles).
2) If yes, check whether recommendations were approved/enqueued for annotation and whether annotation completed.
3) If annotation incomplete and slice is critical, escalate for emergency annotation credit and run an interim limited-synthesis with max_perturb=0.05.
4) If annotation complete but detection power did not improve, open a root-cause with hypothesis: (a) seed selection bias, (b) insufficient diversity, (c) quantization collapse.
